Processing script data/paraguay_2021_women.do, Bookmark 9: partner.
note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the .do builds item = "P1007_" + line, where line is REG10C's L1007 (or REG10D's L1011 for ex-partner rows), a number-preserving rename of the source line code (core model s3 pattern 2). The data dictionary's value labels for L1007 tie lines 1-24 to text, and L1011's give the same 24 contents in the same order in past tense. NUMBERING TRAP (checked, resolved): the printed questionnaire numbers its rows 1-23 and has NO political-participation row, while the dictionary numbers 24 lines with line 10 = '¿Le ha impedido su participación o limitado su opinión en el ámbito político, comuitario, gremial, comité vecinal, escolar o en los ámbitos en que usted se desenvuelve?'. So questionnaire row k = data line k for k<=9 and data line k+1 for k>=10 (questionnaire row 10 'amenazado verbalmente' = P1007_11 ... row 23 = P1007_24). REG10C has no line 10 at all (lines 1-9, 11-24); REG10D has line 10 (raw Sí/No/NR 62/760/2), which the .do drops. Which numbering the data follow was settled with INE's own CAPI filter flags in REG11A: P1100 (1100F, 'Sí' iff any Sí on the physical/sexual rows) equals 'any Sí on data lines 16-24' in 3217/3217 women with P1100 in {1,6} (432 and 2785), but 'any Sí on lines 15-23' (the questionnaire's printed range applied to the data codes) disagrees in 118; P1102 (1102F, rows 1-15 vs 1-14) disagrees in 3/2787 under lines 1-15 and 15/2787 under lines 1-14. The manual's 1100F text also uses the 24-line numbering ('tema del 16 al 24'). The manual's own 'Tipos de violencia' table uses a third, 21-row numbering (omits 'echarla de la casa' and 'encerrada') and was not used. POOLING (1007/1011): the .do stacks REG10D's 1011 (women with no current partner, about the ex-husband/ex-partner/ex-boyfriend, past tense) under the same P1007_<line> codes as REG10C's 1007 (current partner, present perfect), keeping current-partner answers for the 1 woman in both registers. REG10C 2403 women, REG10D 824 (823 after the overlap); live 3224 ids. As in batch_601 (control), item_text ships the 1007 current-partner wording (about 74% of respondents) and the 1011 variant is disclosed here and in public_note, not shipped. 1011 stem: 'Desde que inició la relación que tuvo con su ex esposo, ex pareja o ex novio:'; rows are the same acts in the imperfect ('¿Él tomaba decisiones...', '¿La insultaba...', '¿La empujaba o le estiraba del pelo?' ...), row 24 reads '¿La obligaba su ex esposo o ex pareja a tener relaciones sexuales con otra persona, con o sin la presencia de él?', and row 19 keeps '¿Ha intentado asfixiarla o la ha quemado a propósito?' unchanged. RESP: the .do sets 9 (NR) to missing and recodes (6=1)(1=2), so source 1 Sí / 6 No becomes live 1 = No, 2 = Sí; option_text is keyed to the LIVE codes (1 No, 2 Sí). Route 9: raw REG10C+REG10D counts (line 10 and the overlap woman's REG10D rows dropped) recoded equal live resp 1/2 in 46/46 item x resp cells; the unrecoded reading matches 0/46. Live 1/2 (= raw No/Sí): P1007_1 2922/302, _2 3010/214, _3 2578/645, _4 2947/276, _5 2797/427, _6 2848/375, _7 3020/203, _8 3152/72, _9 2971/252, _11 2945/278, _12 3001/221, _13 3178/45, _14 3083/141, _15 2852/372, _16 2920/299, _17 3023/201, _18 3042/182, _19 3087/135, _20 3166/58, _21 3162/62, _22 3170/54, _23 3053/170, _24 3222/1. Dropped NR (9): REG10C 1-4 per line, REG10D 2-4 per line. Live 74134 rows (the .do asserts 74134), per-item n 3219-3224. P1007_24 has a single Sí in the whole table (REG10C 1, REG10D 0). validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (23 items, resp {1,2}). TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the questionnaire's 1007 stem 'Desde que inició su relación actual con su esposo, pareja o novio:' joined to each row's question, with the row number dropped and line-break hyphens joined (men-sajes, segui-do, apare-cido, ence-rrada, ma-tarse, que-mado, degra-dantes, re-laciones, perso-na). Diffed against the dictionary's L1007 labels: 20/23 identical; the 3 differences are dictionary typos not shipped ('La ha ha amenazado' line 12, 'amezado' line 13, 'amenazándole' line 15 where the questionnaire has 'amenazándola'). instructions left blank: the 1001G read-aloud framing precedes 1002 (shipped as instructions in batch_601), not 1007, and ex-partner women heard 1004G instead; the manual's 'Recuerde que...' line is interviewer-facing. option_text = the questionnaire's 'Sí' / 'No' (dictionary agrees); no row for NR 9. The 1008-1010 follow-ups (frequency, severity, last 12 months) are not in this table. Single section_id, no section_prompt. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INE publishes the ENSIMUP in Spanish only; all English produced by IRW (the Spanish rows have no explicit subject after row 1 and are rendered with 'he'; 'armas blancas' rendered 'bladed weapons'). public_note: The English wording for this table was produced by IRW, not by INE Paraguay, which publishes the ENSIMUP 2021 in Spanish only; women with no current partner (about a quarter of respondents) answered the past-tense version about their ex-husband, ex-partner or ex-boyfriend (question 1011), pooled under the same item codes; the item codes follow INE's data dictionary, so from P1007_11 on they are one higher than the row numbers printed in the questionnaire (which omits a political-participation row, line 10, that is not in this table); and the response codes were reversed in processing so that 1 = No and 2 = Sí (yes), unlike the questionnaire's 1 = Sí, 6 = No.
